description: Characterized arm of the rain instrument: the Chancellor.
notes: The **treatment arm**: `projectile_rain_boss` with a character in it.

**`hazard` breaks the pair, and that is a decision rather than an oversight (designer, 2026-07-29: books that fly across the arena, and that hurt).** Everything else in this file exists to make the two arms the same fight; a hazard the control does not have is a mechanical difference, so a result measured between the arms can no longer be attributed to characterization alone. `tests/chancellor.test.ts` names it as the one licensed exception rather than dropping the check, so nothing *else* can drift in behind it. Two ways back if the pair is wanted intact: give the control the same hazard with the shelves undressed, or set `count` to 0. It needs an ADR line in `docs/DECISIONS.md` before any result from this pair is cited.

Selecting between these two encounters *is* the condition. That is deliberately not a boolean somewhere in the renderer: `lab/session.ts` keys every attempt by `combatId|encounterId|slowMoId`, so an encounter pair is the one shape that records which arm ran without a new axis to thread — the operator cannot forget to write it down, and a run's own record says which side of the comparison it belongs to.

Everything mechanical must match the control: same arena, same player start, same spawn position, same wave timing, and a boss whose stats are spread from the control's object in `lab/config.ts`. Only `archetype` differs, which is what carries silhouette, colour and name — and it is the reason those three did not each need their own flag.

The room is written out rather than spread from the control because the literal is what the reader compares; `tests/chancellor.test.ts` asserts the two are identical field for field apart from the archetype, so drift fails a test rather than depending on a spread nobody re-reads. An arm that quietly stops matching its control is the one defect that would make every result from this pair meaningless while still looking like it ran.
